summary: Multiplexed fanout causing intermittent GPU starvation in dedicated pool; noisy adjacent tenant suspected
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (LuminaSearch) observed sustained p99 and significant throughput drop on their dedicated pool during a midday peak window. Symptoms align with rapid small-stream fanout from a subset of sessions plus elevated prefetch activity leading to intermittent GPU slot attachments failing and autoscaler failing to converge.

Impact:
- Customer reports 30-45% drop in completed tokens/sec for chat endpoints for ~15 minute windows, repeated three times across the morning.
- Elevated API p50->p99 variance and increased 429s from the route tied to their reserved capacity.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lumina-dedicated-usw-3
- Region: us-west
- Models: gpt-open-7b (primary), opt-6.7b (fallback)
- Tenant type: dedicated (reserved capacity)

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) Customer runs high fanout multiplexed chat workload (many short-lived streams with keepalives).
2) Prefetchs for long contexts and KV cache warmups trigger background snapshot sweeps.
3) Autoscaler attempts to add ephemeral slots but sees rapid slot fragmentation due to many small concurrent connections.
4) Some attach attempts time out, triggering fallback routing and a cascade where throughput collapses for allocated slots.

Observed behavior:
- Attach latency spike from 200ms baseline -> multi-second percentiles in the allocator dashboard (see dashboard link).
- GPU attach failures produce 5xx and 429s intermittently.
- Telemetry shows a neighboring tenant with a burst of short streams and aggressive prefetching during the same window.

Expected behavior:
- Dedicated pool should preserve throughput for the committed tenant; autoscaler and allocator should avoid short-lived connection fanout starving slot allocation.

Logs & dashboards:
- Allocation dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/alloc/allocator-usw?orgId=1&var=pool=lumina-dedicated-usw-3
- Autoscaler trace: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/autoscale/heap?panelId=7&from=now-1h&to=now
- Sample logs (truncated): allocator ERROR attach_timeout tenant=lumina session=abc123 attach_attempts=5

Requester notes:
- Customer asked for short-term mitigation and longer-term guardrails to prevent noisy adjacent tenants from impacting reserved capacity.
comments: 2026-03-10 03:18 UTC - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and paging allocator and autoscaler owners. Notified customer and scheduled immediate teleconference at 03:30.

2026-03-10 03:30 UTC - SRE (Marcus): Observed attach latency spike correlated with a high-count of short-lived connections from tenant 'coast-data' in the same reserved pool. Recorded logs and started temporary token-based throttling for that tenant at 03:32 UTC.

2026-03-10 04:00 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer confirms partial recovery after throttling; throughput restored to ~85% of baseline. Customer requested permanent guardrails and visibility into noisy tenant behavior.

2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - Eng (Liam O'Neill): Allocator PR opened to add short-stream dampening to attach scoring algorithm. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/2543. Investigation continues into prefetch and snapshot sweep coupling.
2026-03-11 14:05 UTC - Product (Maya Singh): Logged follow-up to evaluate default per-pool soft throttles and to add an alert if ephemeral attach failures exceed 5% for >10m. Linked to roadmap item.

2026-03-12 08:30 UTC - Support (Aisha): Moving ticket to In Progress; mitigation applied and engineering changes in review. Monitoring for 72h window before close and will provide post-incident notes to customer.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Short-lived multiplexed streams from adjacent tenant cause scheduler slot fragmentation and increase attach contention. Evidence: connection histogram shows 60% of sessions <10s during the window.

Hypothesis 2: Background prefetch/snapshot sweeps from the noisy tenant amplify NVMe/cached IO causing attach timeouts on some GPU hosts. Evidence: IO wait increases correlate with attach timeouts in host metrics.
Test performed: Temporarily rate-limited 'coast-data' tenant prefetch and applied per-tenant ephemeral connection cap; attach failure rate dropped from 6.8% -> 1.1% within 3 minutes.
Telemetry: Allocator logs show repeated quick-release of prefetched leases; autoscaler shows backoff loops because slot attach failures caused it to under-provision visible capacity.
Next steps: Stabilize short-stream dampening in allocator scoring, add per-tenant prefetch rate limiter, and create an alert rule for attach_failure_rate > 2% sustained 5m.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: Temporary per-tenant prefetch throttles and ephemeral-connection caps for the noisy adjacent tenant were applied at 2026-03-10T03:32:00Z, restoring majority of Lumina's throughput to ~85-95% of baseline. Engineering changes (allocator short-stream dampening + autoscaler alert) are under PR and in review (see related PRs).

Post-incident follow-ups:
- Ship allocator scoring fix (PR 2543) and autoscaler alerting change in next patch release.
- Add a console view to surface noisy-tenant signals (prefetch rate, avg session length) per-pool for dedicated customers.
- Schedule a debrief and publish a short postmortem to the customer and Confluence.

Status: Mitigation in place; permanent fixes in review. Monitoring window set 72h; will update when PRs merge and release occurs.
